messages.subject: How to interpret lp__?
parts:
Hi all, STAN newbie here:

I'm trying to figure out how to interpret the lp__ value from a STAN model. I know from page 8 of the rstan manual that it is "the logarithm of the (unnormalized) posterior density." What does this mean? Is it the likelihood of the data given the model integrated over the posterior density of the model parameters?

Thank you!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: How to interpret lp__?
parts:
It depends on how you write the model. Suppose you have
data y and parameters vector. exp(lp__) is proportional
to p(theta|y).

In practice, if you only use sampling statements (~), lp__
will be the log joint, log p(y,theta), less any constant
terms that only depend on y.

If you use increment_log_prob(normal(log(x,mu,sigma)), then
you don't drop normalizing terms compared to x ~ normal(mu,sigma);.
But they sample over the same posterior.

- Bob
